steps.description: Read /eval-full-32-without-python-enrichment-only-1/data/inputs/results/de_results.csv (12,000 genes x 8 columns; DESeq2 results for treated vs control) in Python. Report the actual column names found rather than assuming them, mapping them to: gene symbol, base_mean, log2_fold_change, its standard error, raw p-value and adjusted p-value. Produce (a) a signed ranking vector over every gene with a non-NA test statistic — use the shrunken log2 fold change if the table provides one, otherwise sign(log2FC) * -log10(p-value), breaking ties deterministically and dropping NA/infinite entries with a count of how many were dropped; (b) a significant-gene list at padj < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 1, and also a looser padj < 0.1 list, reporting the size of each and splitting up- vs down-regulated; (c) the ORA background = all genes with a non-NA adjusted p-value (i.e. genes that survived DESeq2 independent filtering), with the count of NA-padj genes reported separately. Also cross-check that the 12,000 gene rows correspond to the gene symbols in the counts matrix /data/inputs/counts/counts.csv. Write ranked list, DE gene lists and background to CSV for the next step, plus a summary of counts and a volcano plot.

steps.description: Using the ranked gene list and DE/background lists from T1S1, run hallmark pathway enrichment in Python. Reference data needed: the human (Homo sapiens) MSigDB hallmark gene-set collection in gene-symbol space — resolve it from the environment's reference store at run time and confirm it contains ~50 HALLMARK_* sets before use; the file is tab-separated GMT with the set name first, a source URL second, then HGNC member symbols, so the URL field must be dropped when parsing. Primary analysis: pre-ranked GSEA (gseapy.prerank) over the full signed ranking, min set size 10, max 500, at least 1000 permutations, fixed random seed, reporting NES, nominal p, FDR q, set size and leading-edge genes for all 50 sets. Secondary/sensitivity analysis: over-representation of the padj<0.05 significant gene list against the tested-gene background (gseapy.enrich with the local GMT), run separately for up- and down-regulated genes, with Benjamini-Hochberg FDR across the 50 sets. Report the full 50-set result table sorted by NES, flag sets with FDR < 0.25 and separately FDR < 0.05, and state explicitly where GSEA and ORA agree and disagree. Produce a bar/dot plot of NES for the top enriched sets (coloured by FDR) and GSEA running-enrichment plots for the top 3 up and top 3 down sets. If the hallmark collection cannot be resolved in the reference store, stop and report that rather than substituting a different collection.
acceptance_criteria: A full 50-row hallmark result table with NES, nominal p, FDR q, effective set size and leading-edge genes is written to CSV.
Enriched sets are reported with direction (positive NES = up in treated/lesional, negative = up in control) and FDR, at both the 0.25 and 0.05 thresholds.
ORA results for up- and down-regulated gene lists against the tested background are reported alongside, with agreement/disagreement versus GSEA stated.
Plots produced: NES summary plot for top sets and running-enrichment plots for the top 3 up and top 3 down sets.
The organism and set count of the hallmark collection actually used are stated in the output.

plan.title: Hallmark enrichment of AD lesional vs control DE
plan.analytical_narrative:
The research question asks only which MSigDB hallmark pathways are enriched in the treated (atopic dermatitis lesional skin) versus control contrast, and explicitly instructs starting from the existing differential expression results. The persisted profile shows a DESeq2 results table already computed for exactly that contrast (/data/inputs/results/de_results.csv, 12,000 genes x 8 columns, with gene symbol, base_mean, log2_fold_change and shrunken/SE plus p-values), alongside the raw Salmon counts (12,000 x 13, i.e. gene symbol column + 12 samples) and a 12 x 2 metadata table with 6 treated vs 6 control, unpaired, single batch. Because a valid DE table exists, no re-running of DESeq2 is planned; the analysis is enrichment only.

The plan has one short track. T1S1 sanitises and ranks the supplied DE table: it verifies the column names actually present, checks the gene symbol space against the HGNC symbols used by the staged human hallmark GMT, quantifies the overlap, and builds a single signed ranking statistic for GSEA (preferring the shrunken log2 fold change if present, otherwise sign(log2FC) * -log10(pvalue)) plus a threshold-based DE gene list and the full tested-gene background for ORA. It also records how many genes are NA / independently filtered, since DESeq2 sets padj to NA for filtered genes and those must be excluded from the ORA background properly rather than treated as non-significant.

T1S2 runs the enrichment itself against the 50 MSigDB human hallmark sets. Preregistered primary readout is pre-ranked GSEA over all ranked genes (uses the whole distribution, robust to an arbitrary fold-change cutoff, and appropriate for a 6v6 design where few genes may clear padj < 0.05); ORA on the padj-significant gene list against the tested background runs alongside as a sensitivity check, with agreement between the two reported explicitly. Both are FDR-corrected across the 50 sets and reported with leading-edge / overlapping gene members so that a hit can be traced back to actual genes.

Two caveats are carried through rather than analysed away. First, sample_01 has a library size about 4x below the median; this does not affect enrichment directly, because we start from the provided DE table, but it means the upstream effect sizes for that comparison may be noisier than nominal, and the report must say so rather than assume clean input. Second, we did not recompute DE, so the hallmark result inherits every modelling choice of the supplied DESeq2 table. Both steps use Python only, per the user constraint — gseapy (installed, 1.3.1) provides both prerank and enrichr-style ORA against a local GMT, with decoupler available as a cross-check. The human hallmark GMT (50 HALLMARK_* sets, HGNC symbols) is confirmed present in the reference store and matches the organism (Homo sapiens) and identifier space (gene symbols) of the input.
